target.title: fix: scope refresh-row disabling to the provider being refreshed
target.body: ## Problem Clicking Refresh (or ⌘R) in one provider's menu disabled the "Refresh" row for *every* provider, not just the one being refreshed. In unmerged mode each provider's own menu showed a greyed row; in merged mode switching tabs showed the same. Since only the clicked provider actually refreshes, the greyed rows implied work that wasn't happening. The manual-refresh path was also globally single-flight, so a second provider's refresh was silently dropped while the first was in flight. ## Cause `isRefreshActionInFlight(for:)` returned early on `manualRefreshTask != nil`, and `startManualRefresh(for:)` guarded on that same single global task. Both were provider-agnostic, even though the store already tracks refreshes per provider via `refreshingProviders`. ## Change **Scoped refresh tracking** (initial commit) - Replace the single `manualRefreshTask` with `manualRefreshTasks: [ManualRefreshScope: Task]`, where `ManualRefreshScope` is `.global` (the all-providers ⌘R / merged-overview refresh) or `.provider(p)`. - The disable gate now reflects only the target provider's own refresh. A `.global` refresh still disables every row. - `startManualRefresh` guards per scope, so different providers refresh concurrently instead of blocking each other. The store already supported this (`refreshingProviders` is a set); only the controller serialized it. - `MenuCardRefreshMonitor` tracks in-flight providers as a set plus a global flag, so the "Refreshing…" subtitle and frozen-layout freeze stay scoped per provider. **Review-driven hardening** (`7ac1b3c1` + `b7b7c20e`, addressing Copilot + ClawSweeper + an independent review) - **Frozen-card retention**: the monitor's merge was new-wins, so a second provider's refresh re-captured the first provider's mid-refresh card and overwrote its frozen snapshot, producing the visible jump the freeze exists to prevent. Now old-wins (`{ existing, _ in existing }`): a provider already in flight keeps the card it froze when it began. - **Global/provider exclusivity**: `startManualRefresh` now blocks a `.global` refresh while any per-provider task exists, and vice versa. Two *different* providers still refresh concurrently. This prevents duplicate fetch work and is consistent with the merged-overview row being greyed whenever any manual refresh runs. - **Overview row no longer flickers**: the merged-overview Refresh row now reflects any in-flight manual refresh, including a per-provider refresh's post-fetch status/token/credits tail (after `refreshingProviders` has cleared). Previously it toggled greyed→enabled→greyed across phases. - **Deterministic test accessors**: `manualRefreshTask` / `manualRefreshProvider` are test-only and now return a value only when unambiguous (the `.global` task, or the single task when exactly one is in flight), otherwise `nil`. Moved to `StatusItemController+Actions`. ## Design note: chosen overview semantics The overview Refresh row triggers an all-providers refresh, so it is greyed whenever *any* manual refresh is in flight, and a global refresh cannot start on top of a per-provider one. Individual provider rows stay independently enabled (each reflects only its own refresh). This was a conscious choice over "overview stays enabled throughout"; it avoids both the flicker and duplicate concurrent all-providers work. ## Tests Rewrote the refresh-row tests that asserted the old blanket behavior (e.g. refreshing Claude greying the Codex row) to the scoped semantics. Added coverage for: - a second provider refresh keeping the first provider's frozen card (`concurrent manual refreshes keep each provider's frozen card`), - one provider's refresh not blocking another (`refreshing one provider does not block refreshing another`), - the overview staying busy through a per-provider tail and blocking a global refresh (`overview stays busy through a provider refresh tail and blocks a global refresh`), - a provider manual refresh only greying its own tab (`StatusMenuSwitcherRefreshTests`). Affected suites: `StatusMenuPersistentRefreshTests`, `StatusMenuSwitcherRefreshTests`, `StatusMenuMergedOverviewRefreshTests` (~50 tests). CI runs the full sharded macOS suite. ## Validation `swift build` and `swiftlint --strict`/`swiftformat` clean locally. CI: lint + linux-cli builds pass; macOS test shards are the authoritative runtime check (local Xcode 27 beta cannot load Sparkle.framework at test runtime, so runtime verification is deferred to CI's Xcode 26.x). ## Proof The two screenshots below show the *before* state (one provider's refresh greying unrelated rows). Fresh after-state proof showing one provider's Refresh row disabled while a sibling stays enabled is pending; requesting maintainer-side capture via Mantis, or I can attach one on request. --- when refreshing claude code, other providers like cursor should not be greyed (before):
